summary:
FMLink profiles the conversion of the former Anthem North Building in Richmond, Virginia into Kinsale North, a Class A office for insurer Kinsale Insurance. The 1960s concrete midcentury structure sits across the street from Kinsale's existing campus and was chosen because it offered size and proximity without leaving the campus. Roughly 280,000 square feet were adapted to support more than 900 employees, who moved in during November 2025.

Design firm Baskervill worked with construction manager Hourigan under a design-build model, with Introba leading mechanical and plumbing. Design began in late summer 2023 and demolition started in early 2024 before construction documents were complete; early demolition packages and phased GMP releases let design and construction run in parallel toward substantial completion in late 2025.

Architecturally, a new two-story entry volume on the north side gives Kinsale a clearer identity and primary entrance, responding to site slope with entries at different levels. The lower level holds mission-critical infrastructure including switchgear and generators serving both North and South campus buildings. Offices and amenities occupy floors one through four, with upper floor plates averaging over 40,000 square feet. The original 1966 precast facade was fully removed and replaced with metal stud framing, storefront, selective curtain wall and spandrel panels.

The central technical decision was retaining and extending the existing Tate Access Floors ConCore 1000 PosiLock raised access floor, upgraded to ConCore 1250 PosiLock. Underfloor routing supports data, power and HVAC distribution and absorbed slab irregularities, with pedestals mostly around 20 inches and some near 30 inches, avoiding costly slab correction. About 75 to 80 percent of each floor plate uses carpet tile to preserve plenum access; hard surfaces appear selectively in restrooms, coffee bars and amenity spaces. Underfloor air delivery required rethinking acoustics, wall construction and confidentiality planning, with some walls extended fully to slab.
